text:
All 25 tests now pass with `python3 -m unittest`. I started with the grep for `self` as you asked. I didn't edit any tests. There were seven separate defects, each a one-line fix:

| File | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `taskflow/queue.py` | `sort_key` was `(seq, -priority)`, so insertion order beat priority. | Changed to `(-priority, seq)`. |
| `taskflow/retry.py` | `should_retry` used `attempts_made < max_attempts - 1`, which allowed one attempt too few. | Changed to `attempts_made < max_attempts`. |
| `taskflow/config.py` | `deep_merge` recursed as `deep_merge(value, result[key])`, so the defaults overrode the task's own values. | Swapped the arguments. |
| `taskflow/statemachine.py` | `batch_order_ok` required priority to be non-decreasing, but its docstring says non-increasing. | Changed `>=` to `<=`. |
| `taskflow/scheduler.py` | `_cascade_skip` only skipped direct dependents. | It now uses `dag.transitive_dependents`. |
| `taskflow/events.py` | `_prefix_matches` had its arguments reversed, so prefix subscriptions never matched. The history therefore never recorded terminal outcomes. | Changed to `topic.startswith(prefix + ".")`. |
| `taskflow/resources.py` | `ResourcePool.release` did `self.used -= 1` instead of `-= cost`. Multi-unit resources leaked, which stalled the resource pipelines. | Changed to `-= cost`. |

Fixing the queue, retry, merge and batch-guard bugs let the retry and priority tests through. That exposed the cascade, event and resource defects, which were hidden behind them.
